published_statement: Fewster-Olum-Pfenning gr-qc/0609007 p.10: '[the] spacetime obtained by periodically identifying Minkowski space along the z-direction. The ground state of the massless, minimally coupled scalar field on this (globally hyperbolic) spacetime has renormalized stress tensor <T_ab> = (pi^2/(90 L^4)) diag(-1, 1, 1, -3) (24) where L is the periodicity length. It is readily verified that the (A)NEC is violated along any null geodesic with a nonzero z-component of velocity, i.e., for those which wind around the compact direction. On the other hand, the (A)NEC is obeyed along complete null geodesics with zero velocity in the z-direction ... null geodesics which wind round the cylinder are not achronal.' p.11: 'distant interactions or boundary conditions apparently do not help to produce ANEC violations. For example, Casimir plates would not seem to be useful to support a wormhole ... because of the need to get through the plate.' Kuo-Ford gr-qc/9304008 eqs.(3.32)-(3.33): '... = -(zeta(4)/(pi^2 L^4)) diag[1,-1,-1,3] ... we have excluded the n = 0 term, since it is just the contribution from the Minkowski vacuum. Since zeta(4) = pi^4/90, <:T_00(x):> = -pi^2/(90 L^4).' GJW 1608.05687 sec. 5 (the tree's context, prose only): 'the negative ANE could be understood as coming from the Casimir effect associated to the cycle in space ... Of course, the effect would be enhanced if the signals sent between the black holes were directed and amplified (otherwise the Casimir energy would be extremely tiny if the black holes were far apart).'
published_hypotheses: H1 field content: ONE free, massless, real scalar (minimally coupled; in flat space without boundaries the conformal improvement adds nothing since <phi^2> is constant). Other fields change the coefficient (EM: 2 dof).

H2 geometry: flat Minkowski space with ONE periodic spatial identification of length L, infinite and homogeneous in the transverse directions; the density is UNIFORM. No wormhole, no curvature, no throat.
H3 state: the ground (vacuum) state of the identified spacetime, zero temperature; renormalised by subtracting the Minkowski (n = 0) term.

H4 the negative quantity is the energy density T_00 = -pi^2/(90 L^4); the null-null component is -4 pi^2/(90 L^4) along geodesics that wind the compact direction and ZERO along null geodesics transverse to it (FOP p.10); ANEC is violated only on non-achronal (winding) geodesics.

H5 semiclassical: <T_ab> is an expectation value; Kuo-Ford's paper is precisely about the fluctuations around it, which are not small in general (their abstract: semiclassical theory 'a good approximation only when the fluctuations in the stress tensor are small').

H6 (GJW context) the flat-space Casimir reading of the cycle is a discussion-section remark with no computation; GJW state the undirected effect is 'extremely tiny' at large separation and that directing/amplifying the signals would enhance it.

later_literature.ref: Maldacena, Milekhin & Popov, arXiv:1807.04726v3, 'Traversable wormholes in four dimensions' (2018; v3 2020)
later_literature.what: Realises GJW's 'directed' Casimir enhancement: massless charged fermions in the magnetic field of near-extremal magnetic black holes have a lowest Landau level of degeneracy q, giving q two-dimensional fields that move along closed field lines through the wormhole; 'A two dimensional fermion on a circle gives rise to a negative Casimir-like vacuum energy' (p.4), E = -q/(6l) on the flat cylinder, net -q/(8l) after the conformal-anomaly cancellation (eqs 5.24-5.27, re-derived here), and a self-consistent semiclassical solution with l = 16 r_e^3/(G_N q) (5.31) and no amplification factor. The negative energy scales as q/(length) with two independent lengths, not as a single-length L^-4 density -- so '4.39e71 short' is a property of the undirected single-scalar flat-cycle model, not of Casimir support as such. It does NOT establish a metre-scale case: the SM embedding needs d below the electroweak length (p.5), the wormhole is 'long' (pi l > d; ~2.35 d at large d, p.19-20) and fragile ('not safe for human travelers', p.19), and the N_f = 1 analysis stops at d ~ q^3 l_p (p.24).

later_literature.what: Scalar-field Casimir tensor in a long R x S^2 throat: 'sufficient magnitude to stabilise a long-throated wormhole far larger than the Planck scale, at least in principle' via a^2 = l_p^2 (L/a) ln(a/a0)/(360 pi) (eq.68), which breaks the single-length Planck argument (p.1, footnote 2); BUT T_kk = 0 for null rays parallel to the throat (eq.70), 'this shortfall prevents us from stabilising' the static wormhole; it does slow collapse (closure time ~ L^{2/3}). It narrows the tree's reading of the Planck landing as independent evidence, and on its own terms it does not supply a metre-scale corridor either.

Asymptotically flat traversable wormholes from Casimir-like energy of a compact cosmic string wrapping the cycle through the wormhole; integrated null energy exponentially small for non-extremal backgrounds, traversability 'exponentially fragile'. lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. The formula is a theorem of free QFT on a flat identified spacetime, and the only numerical inputs are hbar, c (exact since 2019) and G (22 ppm); the tree's constants are current and CODATA 2022 moves the gain by 6e-10 relative. No experiment measures a periodic-identification Casimir density, and the plate-force measurements (sibling audit) confirm the Lifshitz/ideal framework, with every real-material correction REDUCING |rho|. So for this result the authors lacked no DATUM that changes the conclusion: evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis on the data side. What was missing in 2016 (GJW remark) was a CONSTRUCTION, not data: GJW named 'directed and amplified' signals without quantifying them, and the tree quantified only the undirected single-scalar version. MMP (2018) and Butcher (2014) supply constructions whose negative energy does not follow the single-length pi^2/(90 L^4) law; that is a hypothesis the tree's model drops (H2), not an inaccuracy in the older mathematics. Neither construction reaches metre-scale separation with Standard Model content (MMP: d below the electroweak length; Butcher: static wormhole not stabilised, metre-long throat has radius ~6e-25 m), so having the later results narrows the class the tree's number describes without overturning the tree's metre-scale refusal.
grade_evidence: The external result STANDS on its hypotheses: rho = -pi^2 hbar c/(90 L^4), <T_ab> = (pi^2/(90 L^4)) diag(-1,1,1,-3), re-derived two independent ways (sympy, exact) and matching FOP eq.(24) and Kuo-Ford eq.(3.33) as read; the tree's numbers (2.167e-28 Pa, 9.505e43 Pa, 4.3866e71 D^2, 0.0934 l_P) reproduce exactly and equal the closed form 360 D^2/(pi l_P^2); no datum has moved (CODATA 2022: 6e-10). The TREE'S USE is broader than the result: (1) phase1.py:403-404 quotes the figure without its model hypotheses -- one free scalar, flat transversely infinite uniform density, a single length D, cycle 2D -- and gjw.py:94-100 reads the resulting Planck landing as independent evidence when it is forced by the single-length model (D4); later literature (Butcher 2014, MMP 2018, read) shows Casimir-type sources with two lengths or 2D-reduced modes that escape that law, so '4.39e71 short' holds for the undirected flat-cycle scalar model, not for Casimir support as a class. (2) DISCREPANCY: energy density divided into a T_kk threshold; the winding-direction T_kk is 4|rho| (gain 1.097e71 D^2). (3) DISCREPANCY: the figure is attached to the 'Casimir corridor' (plate model, gain 2.193e71 at 1 m) though computed for GJW's cycle. None is WRONG: every named variant stays at 5e70-3.5e72 at 1 m (check F1), the metre-scale refusal is not overturned by any construction read (MMP's SM embedding stops below 2e-19 m), and phase1's ranking does not depend on the number (Lambda None).
